subject: Biochemistry
vignette: A 5-year-old unvaccinated boy is brought with fever and sore throat. Examination shows a gray adherent pseudomembrane over the tonsils, marked neck swelling, and a muffled voice. Two weeks later he develops heart failure with elevated creatine kinase MB and conduction abnormalities. Cultures grow Corynebacterium diphtheriae.
question: Which of the following best explains the toxin-mediated inhibition of protein synthesis in this patient's cardiac cells?

options.text: ADP-ribosylation of eukaryotic elongation factor 2, preventing translocation
Cleavage of 28S rRNA in the 60S subunit
Binding to the 30S subunit and causing misreading
Prevention of the initiator tRNA from binding the P site

explanation_correct: Diphtheria toxin ADP-ribosylates eukaryotic elongation factor 2, inactivating it and blocking translocation of the peptidyl-tRNA from the A site to the P site. Protein synthesis stops, which explains the toxin-mediated damage to the heart and nervous system. Pseudomonas exotoxin uses the same mechanism, and both are A-B toxins.

explanation_incorrect.B: Cleavage of 28S rRNA is the mechanism of Shiga toxin.
explanation_incorrect.C: 30S misreading is caused by aminoglycosides, which are antibacterial and do not act on human elongation factor 2.
explanation_incorrect.D: Peptidyl transferase inhibition is the mechanism of chloramphenicol and macrolides in bacterial ribosomes.
explanation_incorrect.E: Prevention of initiator tRNA binding is not the mechanism; the toxin acts during elongation.

educationalObjective: Diphtheria toxin ADP-ribosylates and inactivates eukaryotic elongation factor 2, blocking translocation and protein synthesis.
